title: introduce-operator-tenancy-ttl-and-kms-weighted-fallback-guard
author: Marina Kaur
release_notes: Adds operator-scoped TTL on delegated RBAC grants, introduces KMS provider weighted fallback for residency constraints, and hooks audit records with residency-evidence token. No user-visible API changes; rollout gated by feature flag.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers operating in multiple jurisdictions requested two things: (1) tighter temporal limits on operator-scoped delegations to reduce blast radius for cross-tenant operator sessions, and (2) a deterministic, auditable KMS selection strategy when a tenant's preferred KMS region is momentarily unavailable. This PR implements an RBAC v2 time-to-live (TTL) for delegated grants, a small state-machine to manage ephemeral operator leases, and a KMS multi-provider weighted-fallback mechanism that emits residency proof tokens to the audit pipeline.

What this changes (high level): added operator_bound_grant TTL enforcement in the auth service; introduced a lightweight lease service to allocate short-lived operator leases with optional jurisdiction tags; introduced kms-selection strategy service that picks providers by configured weights and residency compatibility; audit-enrichment step attaches a residency_evidence token (signed assertion) to every KMS call and to the generated audit event; feature-flagged rollout: auth.rbacv2.operator_ttl.enabled and kms.fallback.weighted.enabled.

Files touched (high level): auth-service/{policy,lease}-modules, kms-orchestrator/selector, audit-forwarder/enrichment, console/feature-flags, tests/{unit,integration}. Small schema bump to rbacv2 policy protobuf (operator_ttl seconds, lease_id string) with backwards-compatible defaults.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4921) [x] protobuf schema change reviewed [x] unit and integration tests added [x] e2e with private-installer smoke tested [x] feature flags validated in staging [x] docs updated (console & ops runbook).

Testing and CI: unit test coverage +18%, integration tests include operator lease expiry scenario, failover to secondary KMS provider with weight demotion, and audit replay for residency tokens. CI caught a flaky test on the first run (auth lease TTL race), I fixed it by adding a deterministic clock to the lease allocator and re-ran jobs. Final CI status: all checks pass.

Rollout plan: behind two independent feature flags. Step 1 (canary): enable auth.rbacv2.operator_ttl.enabled for 10% of operator traffic in US region; monitor auth.latency, lease.failures, and audit.evidence-missing alerts. Step 2: enable kms.fallback.weighted.enabled in non-production regions to validate provider weight tuning. Step 3: expand to all traffic and remove fallback experimental log. A rollback path exists per-flag.

Security and compliance notes: TTL prevents long-lived operator tokens from being reused; audit enrichment with signed residency_evidence tokens provides cryptographic proof of KMS selection for downstream compliance checks. The weighted fallback honors tenant-level residency constraints: the selector will only consider providers that are residency-compatible or explicitly consented to by tenant metadata.

Related work: touches on SUP-1289 (customer incident where primary KMS region transiently failed) and ENG-4999 (RBAC v2 policy expressiveness extension).
